1. A lecturer wishes to compare the average blood alcohol concentrations in two of her classes.
   She measures the blood alcohol concentrations of students in two of her Monday morning classes.  

   What type of study is this?
	 
    a. Observational study.
    b. Experimental study.
    c. Quasi-experimental study.

  
2. A lecturer wishes to compare the average blood alcohol concentrations in two of her classes, 
   to determine if knowing in advance leads to different mean blood alcohol concentrations.  

   She informs one class on a Friday that she will be measuring the blood alcohol concentrations in students on a Monday morning, 
   but does not tell another of her Friday classes.  

   What type of study is this?
	 
    a. Observational study.
    b. Experimental study.
    c. Quasi-experimental study.
